For each conclusion, it computes the minimal set of features (sufficient statistics) that preserve all predictive information about future observations. If two conclusions yield the same sufficient statistics, they are merged. The system periodically re-evaluates statistics to detect drift.", "scope": {"covers": ["conclusions that are predictively indistinguishable"], "excludes": ["conclusions with different predictive implications despite surface similarity"]}, "forbidden": [{"case": "Two conclusions with identical sufficient statistics lead to different optimal actions in a decision task.", "eval": "program:check_decision_divergence"}], "prose_notes": "This criterion focuses on downstream informational content rather than derivation history.
